Burn geometries onto a regular grid

Source: R/cb_burn.R
cb_burn.Rd

Rasterize polygons, lines, and points onto a regular grid using the controlledburn Rust crate. Polygon interiors are returned as horizontal runs of fully covered cells, and (in coverage mode) boundary cells are returned with their exact coverage fraction.

Usage

cb_burn(
  geom,
  extent,
  dimension,
  coverage = TRUE,
  crs = NA_character_,
  parity = FALSE,
  threads = 1L,
  id_offset = 0L,
  relate = FALSE
)

Arguments

geom

Geometry input. Anything that wk::as_wkb() understands, e.g. a wk_wkb vector, an sf/sfc column, or a list of raw WKB blobs.

extent

Grid extent as c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) (the ordering used by terra::ext()). If missing, the bounding box of geom is used (via wk::wk_bbox()).

dimension

Grid dimensions as c(ncol, nrow). If missing, ncol is 256 and nrow is computed from it so that cells are square in the units of extent (at least 1 row). A single value is taken as ncol, with nrow computed the same way.

coverage

Logical. If TRUE (default) use exact coverage fractions (boundary cells appear in edges). If FALSE use the faster cell-centre ("approx", fasterize-style) rule, which emits runs only.

crs

Optional coordinate reference system as a WKT string (or anything coercible to character). Carried through to cb_materialize() output.

parity

Logical. By default a multi-part geometry gets one record per cell (parts' coverage is summed, and a cell the parts together fill becomes a run), and adjacent runs on a row are coalesced. If TRUE, give the records of the C++ 'controlledburn' core instead: one run per fully covered boundary cell and separate records for each part.

threads

Number of threads, 1 (default) for none, 0 for all available. The result is identical to the serial burn. Threads only pay for large inputs (the crate uses at most one per 8192 units of work), and with more than one thread the input is parsed up front, which uses more memory.

id_offset

Non-negative whole number added to each geometry's position to give its id (and geom_index in notes), so id = id_offset + k for the kth input geometry. Burn consecutive slices of a collection with offsets 0, n1, n1 + n2, ... and join them with cb_combine() to get exactly the burn of the whole collection. Recorded in attribute id_offset.

relate

Logical. If TRUE, also compute the DE-9IM relation of each polygon to the cells its boundary touches and return it as a sixth table, relations; see cb_relate(), which does the same for an existing burn.

Value

An object of class cb_burn: a named list of five data frames with the grid definition stored in attributes (extent, dimension, crs, coverage) and the number of input geometries in n_geom; with relate = TRUE it also has a sixth table, relations. Indices are 1-based and row 1 is the top row; geometry k (input position) gets id = k.

runs

row, col_start, col_end, id: fully covered cells.

edges

row, col, fraction, id: boundary cells, fraction in (0, 1).

lines

row, col, length, id: line length within the cell, CRS units.

points

row, col, id: one row per point inside the grid.

notes

geom_index, message: non-fatal per-geometry problems.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(wk)
sq <- wkt("POLYGON ((2.5 4.5, 6.5 4.5, 6.5 8.5, 2.5 8.5, 2.5 4.5))")
cb_burn(sq, extent = c(0, 10, 0, 10), dimension = c(10, 10))

## defaults: bbox of the geometry, 256 columns, square cells
cb_burn(sq)
} # }
